text: A live filter has less than thirty-three milliseconds to finish one frame. <break time="0.35s" /> Thirty frames a second means about thirty-three milliseconds per frame. <break time="0.35s" /> Look closer: pixels. <break time="0.35s" /> First, a face model, for example MediaPipe, marks four hundred seventy-eight points on the face. <break time="0.35s" /> Then a filter like a bilateral filter scans the skin: edges stay, texture is wiped. Pores, freckles, fine hairs. <break time="0.35s" /> Next, the points are shifted and the image stretches: eyes grow, the jaw narrows. <break time="0.35s" /> Last, light is added and shadows soften. <break time="0.35s" /> It does this thirty times a second, fresh on every frame. <break time="0.35s" /> The face in the filter is a calculated face. <break time="0.35s" /> Real skin has texture. It should.
